14 Four measuring cylinders are filled with the same liquid to the heights shown.
At which position is the pressure the greatest?
A
30 cm
C
30 cm
B
10 cm
10 cm
D

hints: Notice the liquid heights: two cylinders contain $30 \text{ cm}$ and two contain $10 \text{ cm}$ of the same liquid.
Recall liquid pressure depends on depth below the free surface, $p = \rho g h$, not on total volume in the cylinder.
Compare the vertical distance from each dot A, B, C and D down from its own liquid surface, especially B versus D.
walkthrough: Identify the rule: for the same liquid, pressure at a point is $p = \rho g h$, where $h$ is the depth measured down from the free surface.
Point A is on the surface of the 30 cm column, so $h_A = 0$. Point C is on the surface of the 10 cm column, so $h_C = 0$.
Point D is at the bottom of the 10 cm column, so $h_D = 10 \text{ cm}$.
Point B is in the 30 cm column at the same horizontal level as the surface in the 10 cm column. Its depth is $h_B = 30 \text{ cm} - 10 \text{ cm} = 20 \text{ cm}$.
Compare depths: $20 \text{ cm} > 10 \text{ cm} > 0$. Since $\rho$ and $g$ are the same, the largest $h$ gives the largest $p$.

A.explanation: Point A is at the free surface of the 30 cm column, so depth $h = 0$ and gauge pressure is zero.

B.explanation: Point B is about $20 \text{ cm}$ below the surface, the largest depth of the four positions, so $p = \rho g h$ is largest.

C.explanation: Point C is at the free surface of the 10 cm column, so depth $h = 0$ and gauge pressure is zero.

D.explanation: Point D is at the base of the 10 cm column with depth $10 \text{ cm}$, which is less than the depth of B.
